verdict: Seagate's revenue surged 61% to $4.2B and gross margin hit 57% as data-center customers paid up for high-capacity drives — profit more than tripled to $1.76B and free cash flow set a September-quarter record.

kpis.label: Free cash flow
kpis.note: a September-quarter record; cash flow from operations was $1,690M

kpis.label: Gross margin
kpis.note: up from 39.4% a year ago, on pricing and a shift to higher-capacity drives

segments.name: Data Center
segments.note: Drives for cloud and enterprise data centers — 81% of revenue, as reported in the 10-Q market mix, as AI-driven storage demand and pricing lifted sales.

segments.name: Edge IoT
segments.note: Storage for industrial and consumer uses closer to where data is created — 19% of revenue, as reported in the 10-Q market mix.

opex.name: Product development
opex.note: Engineering the next generations of high-capacity drives, including HAMR technology.

opex.name: Marketing & administrative
opex.note: Marketing and administrative costs of running the company.

opex.name: Restructuring
opex.note: Restructuring and other charges, net — small this quarter.

footerNote: Seagate reports its revenue mix by market as percentages (Data Center 81%, Edge IoT 19% in the 10-Q); the dollar amounts shown apply those reported percentages to total revenue. Segment growth rates are derived the same way from the year-ago mix of 80% / 20%.

takeaways.title: Pricing, not just volume, drove growth
takeaways.text: Revenue rose $1.6B year over year, mainly on favorable pricing and more nearline exabytes shipped (198 of 220 total) as data-center demand for mass-capacity drives strengthened.

takeaways.title: Margins transformed
takeaways.text: Gross margin jumped from 39.4% to 57.3% in a year on pricing and a mix shift to higher-capacity HAMR-based drives, turning the revenue surge into $1,761M of net income.

takeaways.title: Cash is being used to cut debt
takeaways.text: Seagate retired about $1.2B of debt in the quarter, cutting gross debt to $2.4B (and $1.6B after a further $750M retirement in October), while still returning $568M to shareholders.

oneTimers: $44M net loss from debt transactions, from retiring about $1.2B of debt principal during the quarter.
